extracted.intended_audience: NIH F99/K00 grant reviewers and aging researchers / intervention developers
extracted.subtask_description: Research strategy and methodological standards for an F99/K00 grant studying how physical and social environments, social isolation, and ICT use affect cognitive health in older adults, plus co-design and pilot intervention development. Covers measurement, analysis, trial design, systematic review, mixed-methods, and mentoring/institutional resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical environment measurement (community items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviewers standing in front of respondent’s home rated on a four-point scale (1=none, 4=a lot) the amount of litter on the street, graffiti on buildings and walls, and vacant or deserted houses or stores. A scale score of the community physical condition will be derived from the sum score of the corresponding items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interviewer observations rather than zip-code level census data because interviewer observation can provide more accurate information regarding each participant's physical environment and preserves real-life complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical environment measurement (inside home/building)
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical condition inside the respondent’s home/apartment was assessed by observing existence of peeling paint, evidence of pests, broken furniture, flooring need of repair, tripping hazards, and cluttered room. The inside-home scale score is the sum of these items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These interviewer-observed items form a summed scale score to quantify household physical disorder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social environment (community cohesion) operationalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Social environment operationalized as community cohesion perceived by older adults via three items: whether people in the community know each other very well, are willing to help each other, and can be trusted, measured on a three-point scale (1=agree a lot, 2=agree a little, 3=do not agree). A sum score of the three items (range 3–9) is used as the social environment scale score; higher score indicates more neighborhood cohesion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use respondents' perceived cohesion as the social environment measure; sum the items to produce a continuous score for modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICT use measurement (three-purpose classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: NHATS assessed three types of ICT use: instrumental internet use (shop online, pay bills/banking online), social internet use (went online to visit social network sites in the last month), and internet use for medical purposes (order/refill prescriptions, contact medical providers, handle health insurance matters, get information about one's health conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the three ICT aspects as independent moderators; analyze purpose-specific ICT use (social, instrumental, medical) separately because effects may differ by purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social isolation construct (six dichotomous indicators and thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social isolation constructed with six dichotomous indicators: no marriage/partnership, no family identified to talk about important things, no friend identified to talk about important things, never meeting in person with family/friends in past month, no participation in religious service, and no club/class/organization participation. Scale score is the sum (0–6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coding: higher items indicate more isolation. Interpretive thresholds: scores less than 1 represent least isolated; scores 2–3 indicate somewhat isolated; scores ≥4 indicate social isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: I-CONECT trial social isolation eligibility definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For I-CONECT trial enrollment, social isolation defined as i) Score ≤12 on the 6-item Lubben Social Network Scale (LSNS-6); or ii) Engages in conversations lasting 30 minutes or longer no more than twice per week, per subject self-report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these objective/self-report thresholds to identify socially isolated older adults eligible for the intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive health measurement components
rubrics_metrics.description: Cognitive health assessed via: memory (immediate and delayed word recall), orientation (date, month, year, day of week, naming the President and Vice President), and executive function measured by clock drawing test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these standardized domains to form composite outcomes of cognitive functioning; I-CONECT uses UDS V3 battery cross-validated by NIH Toolbox for detailed neuropsychological assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative data management and basic analytic standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Data management and variable recoding to be conducted using Stata 15 SE. Descriptive univariate analyses are run before model building. Correlations of key variables will estimate effect sizes and detect potential multicollinearity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a standard analytic pipeline (cleaning → univariate description → checks for multicollinearity/effect sizes) before fitting multivariable models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sampling weights for representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Sampling weight will be applied to models to match the representativeness of the racial/ethnic groups as designed in the sampling strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate NHATS sampling weights in all inferential models to correct for complex survey design and ensure population-representative estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longitudinal path analysis modeling specifications (Paper 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper 1 will employ longitudinal path analysis to model longitudinal relationships between physical environments, social environment, and social isolation (H1–H3). NHATS wave 5 physical and social environment variables will be included to predict social isolation in wave 9, controlling for baseline social isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify temporal ordering, include baseline controls, and use path modeling to estimate direct and indirect relationships across waves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longitudinal mediation modeling specifications (Paper 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper 2 will study longitudinal association between wave 5 physical and social environments and cognitive health in wave 9 (H4–H5), with social isolation score in wave 6 hypothesized to mediate the relationship between environmental variables and cognitive health (H6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a temporally sequenced mediation approach (wave5 → wave6 mediator → wave9 outcome) to support causal inference about mediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation and direct-effect modeling for ICT use (Paper 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper 3 will examine direct effects of ICT use for different purposes in wave 5 on social isolation in wave 9 (H7–H8) and model the moderating effect of different purposes of ICT use at baseline on the longitudinal association between baseline physical/social environments and wave 9 social isolation (H9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test both main effects and interaction terms (environment × ICT use purpose) to evaluate buffering or exacerbating roles of ICT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic review methods and quality assessment standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic review methods will follow PRISMA guidelines; the review procedure will be registered. A librarian and the sponsor team will help formulate search terms, identify electronic databases, and specify inclusion/exclusion criteria. At least two reviewers will independently evaluate studies, extract data, and meet to resolve disagreements. Research quality will be assessed using GRADE guidelines and GRADEpro software as recommended by the Cochrane Collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to PRISMA and GRADE standards: preregister, use librarian-assisted searches, dual independent review and extraction, consensus procedures, and formal evidence grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention development six-step framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Six steps for quality intervention development: 1) defining and analyzing the problem; 2) identifying modifiable factors; 3) deciding on the intervention mechanism; 4) clarify the intervention delivery process; 5) testing and revising the intervention; 6) a more rigorous effectiveness evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan research activities to map onto these steps: dissertation addresses steps 1–2; postdoctoral work addresses steps 3–4; later pilot funding for step 5 and rigorous evaluation for step 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: I-CONECT randomized clinical trial design and intervention dosage
rubrics_metrics.description: I-CONECT is a randomized trial recruiting 160 socially isolated adults aged 75+ at each site (OHSU & UM), randomized to video-chat intervention vs control. Inclusion: age ≥75, consent to MRI if able, socially isolated, adequate vision/hearing, English, normal cognition or MCI. Intervention participants receive computers/internet and video chat with study staff 30 minutes/day, 4 times/week for 6 months (high dose), then 2 times/week for additional 6 months (maintenance). Study staff briefly check in by phone (~10 minutes) with both intervention and control once per week. In-home neuropsych assessments at baseline, 6 and 12 months; MRI at baseline and 6 months if safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use technology provisioning to ensure access, prespecified dose/frequency schedule, blinded/randomized assignment, and standardized assessment time points for effect estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: I-CONECT primary and biomarker outcome measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary outcomes: executive and memory functioning assessed with the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center Uniform Data Set neuropsychological battery (UDS V3), cross-validated by NIH Toolbox. Region-specific structural and functional pre-post changes in the brain are evaluated with MRI. Medical adherence measured with electronic pillboxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair standardized neuropsychological batteries with neuroimaging and objective digital biomarkers (electronic pillbox) to capture multi-domain intervention effects and reduce self-report bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital biomarkers and CART platform measurement standards
rubrics_metrics.description: CART uses ambient and wearable sensors in homes to assess daily activities, walking speed, sleep patterns, mobility, and computer use; these health behavior and physiological data are digital biomarkers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage unobtrusive sensors to obtain high-frequency objective measures, minimize self-report bias, and enable longitudinal detection of change to validate pathways identified in systematic review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus group qualitative methods and sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus groups to be held with older adults at risk of social isolation, recruited purposefully among current I-CONECT participants using a maximum variation strategy to include diverse living environment conditions. Two focus groups per site (one with intervention participants, one with control), targeted 8 participants per group (total N=32). The interview guide informed by ETA concepts and experts. Sessions audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim; transcripts analyzed using inductive content analysis by at least two trained independent coders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use purposeful maximum-variation sampling to capture diverse perspectives; ensure dual independent coding for reliability; audio-record and verbatim transcribe for rigorous qualitative analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed-methods design rationale and integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine qualitative methods (to understand stakeholders’ perspectives, feasibility, culture and contexts) with quantitative studies (to examine associations and mechanisms). A mixed-methods study is used to co-design and refine a technology-facilitated community-based intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate findings from quantitative analyses and qualitative focus groups to synthesize intervention protocol and guide pilot testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus group analysis reliability standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcripts will be analyzed using inductive content analysis method by at least two trained independent coders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple independent coders to ensure coding reliability and resolve discrepancies via consensus or adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert panel consultation and mentoring engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts panel consisting of all sponsors will be convened quarterly to consult on development of the intervention. Sponsors and co-sponsors reviewed and edited multiple drafts and provide ongoing mentorship (weekly meetings mentioned in mentor contributions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish routine expert consultation (quarterly panels) and frequent mentor contact for feedback on scientific rigor, training, and implementation planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of objective medication adherence monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Medication adherence will be measured with electronic pillboxes, a digital biomarker that can eliminate social desirability bias and record exact times participants opened the pillboxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer electronic objective measures over self-report for adherence outcomes; use device timestamps to obtain precise adherence metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling and recruitment targets for trial sites
rubrics_metrics.description: I-CONECT plans to recruit 160 socially isolated adults aged 75+ at each site (OHSU & UM) for randomization between intervention and control arms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefine per-site sample sizes to ensure adequate power and site comparability; apply inclusion criteria consistently across sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for sponsors, mentors, and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors/mentors selected based on extensive research experience in gerontology, intervention design, neuroimaging, mixed-methods, technology-facilitated interventions, and prior mentoring records. USC is the primary F99 site for training resources; OHSU is the prospective K00 training site with specialized infrastructure (OADC, CART).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose mentors with complementary expertise (intervention methods, biostatistics, neuroimaging, mixed-methods, technology) and institutions offering training, pilot funding, and relevant infrastructure to support proposed research and career development.
